title.narrative: Moving learning, knowledge and lessons learned for innovative education towards peace building through classrooms

description.narrative: Comprehensive education (formación integral) is the cross-cutting theme that seeks to motivate students as agents of change, fostering their autonomy, creativity, critical thinking, and ability to influence their communities. In order to support this process of transformation, while considering the importance of analysing, systematising, and evaluating the initiatives carried out, this proposal seeks to build on the efforts made by Computadores para Educar Colombia (governmental insittution), its results, practices, challenges and lessons learned, to develop a new vision and recommendations for action that, while guiding Computadores para Educar's decision-making to transition from delivering computers to build digital citizenship education for peace, generate spaces and mechanisms for consensus building, dialogue, reflection, training and the sharing of knowledge and experiences. This initiative is being carried out by UNESCO within the framework of a larger proposal, ‘Providing technical support for the implementation and positioning of the knowledge management strategy of Computadores para Educar,’ which is coordinated by UNDP and will result in an inter-agency cooperation agreement (UN-UN Agreement). This larger proposal coordinated by the UNDP is organised into five interrelated components, which together guarantee a comprehensive and coherent intervention with the aim of strengthening knowledge management, educational innovation and the institutional positioning of Computers for Education (CPE). These five components are:-Positioning Documents; Technical notes; A general management report; Data analysis; Communications and Participation. Building on the vision of Computadores para Educar on comprensive education and the importance of improving the integration of technologies in education for advancing peace building in, and through education, UNESCO SJO frames this work as an opportunity to follow-up and implement the 2023 Recommendation.
